description: Frozen copy of the new market-indexed (Phase 6D) and AESO (Phase 6C) records as a scrape builds them on 2026-10-30 (dry runs; not yet in an export): BC Hydro 1892, FortisBC Electric 38, Nova Scotia Power RTP-T/RTP-D, NL Hydro 5.1L and IND-NONFIRM, AESO POOL. Used by the representative-model crosswalk tests so every rule is exercised. Never refreshed by CI.

records.name: AESO Pool Price Reference
records.source_page: Pool Price Metadata (ETS Historical Pool Price report)
records.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. AESO publishes no customer tariff. Pool price is the hourly wholesale energy price, the time weighted average of the one-minute system marginal price (ISO rule 201.6), in $ CAD per MWh. It changes every hour, so no number is stored here (shown as Variable); observed prices belong to a market model, never to a tariff. It is an energy-only wholesale reference, not a retail rate: wires, retail energy (Rate of Last Resort or a contract), riders and fees are separate records. The effective date is the date of AESO's pool price metadata document. The record is live only while the ETS Historical Pool Price report posts current hourly prices.

components.source_detail: AESO ETS Historical Pool Price report and its metadata
components.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Hourly pool price, $0.00-$999.99 per MWh, set by the ISO for each settlement hour; hour-ending, Alberta local time. No average or estimate is stored.

records.name: Transmission Service - Freshet Energy (Rate 1892)
records.eligibility: Optional supply for customers taking Electricity under RS 1830, 1828, 2801, 2802, 2821 or 2822 (transmission service) that increase their Electricity usage during the Freshet Period (May 1 to July 31); Integrated Service Area excluding Kingsgate-Yahk and Lardeau-Shutty Bench. The customer must notify BC Hydro by March 1 with expected monthly MWh and planned operational or production changes; BC Hydro supplies it only if it has energy and capacity.
records.market_reference: ICE Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) Peak or Off-Peak weighted average index price (ICE Day Ahead Power Price Report, US dollars converted at the Bank of Canada daily rate), floored at $0/kWh, plus a $3/MWh adder
records.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Applies only to energy above the customer's approved HLH/LLH baselines in the Freshet Period, scaled by the HLH/LLH Net to Gross Ratio and determined after the period ends; all other energy stays on the base transmission schedule, with Billing Demand set by RS 1892's freshet rules. It is an add-on to the base schedule, not a stand-alone building tariff. Not available while taking RS 1880 or if EPA generator-turndown payments apply; the customer may cancel before July 31. Riders shown separately; taxes excluded.

components.tou_period: HLH and LLH of the Freshet Period
components.tou_hours: HLH: 06:00-22:00 Monday-Saturday except statutory holidays; LLH: all other hours
components.market_reference: ICE Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) Peak or Off-Peak weighted average index price (ICE Day Ahead Power Price Report, US dollars converted at the Bank of Canada daily rate), floored at $0/kWh, plus a $3/MWh adder
components.source_detail: Electric Tariff RS 1892; PDF pages 150-160
components.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Variable: the greater of the hourly-applicable ICE Mid-C Peak or Off-Peak weighted average index price and $0/kWh, plus a $3/MWh adder. The adder is part of this formula and is not a separate charge. The index is published in US dollars and converted at the Bank of Canada daily rate. The tariff gives no ICE web address, so the tariff itself is the source link. No average or estimated price is stored.

records.name: Large Commercial Service - Interruptible (Rate 38)
records.eligibility: Non-firm, interruptible pilot service (available until July 31, 2028) for customers whose entire load at one point of interconnection would normally be eligible for Rate Schedule 30 (contract demand 500 kVA or more, primary voltage) or Rate Schedule 31 (industrial loads of 5,000 kVA or more, transmission voltage); subject to FortisBC suitability review and written agreement, a minimum 12-month term, and, for a part-load election, a served portion large enough to qualify for Rate Schedule 30 or 31 itself
records.market_reference: ICE Day Ahead Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) Peak Index (Peak Hours) / Off-Peak Index (Off-Peak Hours), converted to CAD at the daily Bank of Canada rate (FortisBC Rate Schedule 38)
records.source_page: Electric Tariff PDF page 74, Rate Schedule 38 sheet R-38.1; Electric Tariff PDF page 75, Rate Schedule 38 sheet R-38.2; Electric Tariff PDF page 76, Rate Schedule 38 sheet R-38.3; Electric Tariff PDF page 63, Rate Schedule 30 sheet R-30.1; Electric Tariff PDF page 65, Rate Schedule 31 sheet R-31.1
records.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. FortisBC Electric Rate Schedule 38 (pilot; Order G-136-23 (Interim), G-216-24). The energy price follows the ICE Day Ahead Mid-Columbia index hour by hour, so no value is stored and the price is shown as Variable; only the printed Hourly Service Adder and the customer charge adopted from Rate Schedule 30 or 31 carry numbers. No demand charge is published on these sheets. Interruptible service is non-firm and customers must provide five-year hourly load forecasts.

components.source_detail: Electric Tariff PDF page 63, Rate Schedule 30 sheet R-30.1
components.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Rate Schedule 38 sets the monthly Customer Charge equal to the Customer Charge in effect on Rate Schedule 30 (sheet R-30.1) for customers otherwise eligible for Rate Schedule 30; alternative to the Rate Schedule 31 basis, never added to it. Zero ($0.00) when only part of the load is served under Rate Schedule 38 and the firm part is billed on its own schedule.

components.source_detail: Electric Tariff PDF page 65, Rate Schedule 31 sheet R-31.1
components.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Rate Schedule 38 sets the monthly Customer Charge equal to the Customer Charge in effect on Rate Schedule 31 (sheet R-31.1) for customers otherwise eligible for Rate Schedule 31; alternative to the Rate Schedule 30 basis, never added to it. Zero ($0.00) when only part of the load is served under Rate Schedule 38 and the firm part is billed on its own schedule.

components.component_name: Market Energy (ICE Day Ahead Mid-Columbia Index, hourly)
components.market_reference: ICE Day Ahead Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) Peak Index (Peak Hours) / Off-Peak Index (Off-Peak Hours), converted to CAD at the daily Bank of Canada rate (FortisBC Rate Schedule 38)
components.source_detail: Electric Tariff PDF page 75, Rate Schedule 38 sheet R-38.2
components.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Market-indexed, no value stored. Each hour is billed (Energy Taken x (1 + loss rate %)) x (applicable Mid-C Price + Hourly Service Adder), summed over the billing period. The applicable Mid-C Price is the ICE Day Ahead Mid-Columbia Peak Index in Peak Hours and the Day Ahead Mid-Columbia Off-Peak Index in Off-Peak Hours, in $/MWh, used as $0.00/MWh when negative and capped at the Mid-C Price Cap, if any, nominated by the customer in its Service Agreement; converted to CAD at the daily Bank of Canada rate and settled monthly. System losses follow Rate Schedule 109 (not stored here). Conditional: when hourly use is below the customer's forecast load, Energy Taken is the forecast and the customer receives a credit at the lower of the BC Hydro RS 3808 Tranche One Energy rate and the Mid-C market-based rate (Special Provision 3(b); no value published).

components.source_detail: Electric Tariff PDF page 75, Rate Schedule 38 sheet R-38.2
components.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Added to the applicable Mid-C Price in every hour and multiplied with it by Energy Taken x (1 + loss rate %). The printed formula adds 0.0100 to a Mid-C Price quoted in $/MWh without stating the unit conversion, so no combined per-kWh price is calculated.

records.name: One-Part Transmission Real Time Pricing
records.sub_class: large real time pricing transmission voltage
records.eligibility: (1) Customers must make a written request to take service under this tariff. (2) This tariff is available to customers who are served at transmission voltage of 69 kV or higher and have loads of 2,000 KVA or 1,800 kW, and over.
records.market_reference: NSPI actual hourly marginal energy cost (hourly price final twenty minutes before each hour; forecasts supplied to the customer) plus fixed on-peak/off-peak cost adders
records.source_page: One-Part Transmission Real Time Pricing (Schedule B); PDF pages 89, 90, 91
records.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. NS Power One-Part Transmission Real Time Pricing (Schedule B of the approved April 1, 2026 tariff book): optional firm service for loads of 2,000 kVA or 1,800 kW and over, served at transmission voltage of 69 kV or higher. Demand charge: nil. The energy price is NSPI's actual hourly marginal energy cost (value-less 'Variable' line; nothing is estimated) plus fixed on-peak and off-peak cost adders and the DSM and storm riders, each shown separately; no bill total is calculated. No FAM rate is shown: the approved FAM tariff's rate table has no One-Part Real Time Pricing row and its applicability clause exempts only older-named Real Time Pricing tariffs, so applicability is not assumed. Conditions: written request required; minimum service term of twelve months with automatic renewal (30 days' notice before term end); customers served under the Large Industrial Interruptible Rider may switch only as the tariff allows; meter readings reduce by 1.1% where primary metering is used; billed consumption is adjusted for average power factor below 90% lagging; a separate service agreement may be required. The business-rates web page still lists older extra-high/high/distribution-voltage adders and is not used. The adder page is a scan; its OCR text was checked against the page image.

The price for each hour is final twenty minutes before that hour; NSPI sends the customer hourly price forecasts for the next five days by midnight each business day and notifies major changes. The tariff publishes no price series, so no average or estimated price is stored.

records.name: Island Industrial Non-Firm - Non-Thermal Generation Source
records.eligibility: Island Interconnected bulk transmission grid at 66 kV or greater (primary side of the transformation equipment directly supplying the customer), other than a retailer, with a contract with Hydro for firm power and energy; non-firm energy only.
records.market_reference: NYISO Zone A and ISO New England Mass Hub 5 MW calendar-month day-ahead futures (CAD, adjusted for losses and market fees)
records.notes: Provenance: live_parsed. Only the Non-Thermal Generation Source energy charge is modelled; the Thermal Generation Source charge is a fuel-cost formula with no printed price and is not included. The monthly on-peak and off-peak energy charges are market-indexed and stored without a number ('Variable'): for each calendar month Hydro takes the weighted average (by each market's share of the previous month's kWh exports) of the NYISO Zone A and ISO New England Mass Hub 5 MW calendar-month day-ahead futures settlement prices after trading ends on the 19th day of the previous month, converted to Canadian dollars at that day's exchange rate and adjusted for losses and other market fees. The charge is the greater of that rate and the energy charge of Rate No. 2.4L (General Service 1,000 kVA and Over); that floor is not added to it. Hydro informs the customer on the first business day after the 21st of the preceding month and publishes the monthly on-/off-peak prices (cents/kWh) at https://nlhydro.com/electicity-rates/non-firm-rates-customers/. HST is not included.
